title: Control Delivery Is Not Execution: A Reproducible AIREP Boundary Study
description: This dataset and software artifact evaluates a narrow AIREP boundary: whether successful evidence delivery alone establishes that a consumer executed, interpreted, or enforced the delivered control. Across reproducible consumer variants, the study records delivery outcomes separately from consumer-side execution evidence. The bounded result is that delivery success establishes transport to the consumer boundary, while execution and enforcement require independent consumer-side evidence. The release does not claim universal interoperability, production security, or conformance of arbitrary consumers.
